Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original Unknown/no-source score was mislabelled: Sierra Leone has an operational commercial, carrier-neutral IXP (Michcom-IX), established in-country and now also serving Guinea and Liberia. The operator's own site reports around 15 peering member networks across the three countries, while the Internet Society Pulse IXP tracker lists a smaller set of roughly four Sierra Leone-registered ASNs peering, likely reflecting an earlier snapshot. A separate government-led national IXP (SLIXP) completed a feasibility study in August 2025 but is not yet operational. Given the discrepancy in participant counts between sources and the distinction between the existing private/regional exchange and the still-pending national exchange, this is flagged for human review to settle between 'single IXP with limited participation' (3) and 'active IXP with moderate participation' (4); scored conservatively at 3.
revised_comments: Sierra Leone has an operational Internet Exchange Point, Michcom-IX, a carrier-neutral, non-profit exchange operated by Michcom Limited. Established as the country's first IXP, it now also interconnects networks in Guinea and Liberia, with the operator reporting around 15 peering member networks across the three countries. Separately, the Government of Sierra Leone, through the Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation and the Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project, completed a feasibility study in August 2025 for a national Sierra Leone Internet Exchange Point (SLIXP), which remains at the planning and procurement stage.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted legal or regulatory requirements mandating that certain categories of data (personal data, government data, financial data, or critical infrastructure data) be stored within national borders. Central to data sovereignty debates in Africa.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0/Unknown with no source was mislabelled: Sierra Leone does not yet have data localisation or data protection legislation in force, but a Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill completed national validation in November 2025, and Cabinet approved an accompanying National Data Protection Policy in April 2026 authorising the Bill's finalisation and tabling in Parliament. As the framework remains at draft/policy stage rather than enacted law, code 2 (proposed or draft legislation) applies.
revised_comments: Sierra Leone does not currently have enacted data localisation or comprehensive data protection legislation. A Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill completed nationwide stakeholder validation in November 2025, and in April 2026 the Cabinet approved a National Data Protection Policy authorising the repeal of the Right to Access Information Commission Act and the enactment of a unified Data Protection and Right to Access Information Act. The Bill is being finalised with the Attorney-General's office for tabling in Parliament, so the framework remains at the draft/policy stage rather than in force.

Definition: The presence and tier quality of commercial/colocation data center facilities operating in the country. Commercial data centers provide the physical infrastructure for hosting cloud services, content delivery, and enterprise applications domestically.
Comments: No authoritative data center listing (e.g., Cloudscene/DataCenterMap) for Sierra Leone was collected in this run.

revision_notes: Original score of 0/Unknown with no source was mislabelled: Sierra Leone has at least one confirmed Tier III commercial colocation facility (Afcom, Freetown, self-described Tier III with N+2 redundancy) plus smaller colocation providers (Zoodlabs, Leonecom, per colo.exchange). Telecom operator Orange Sierra Leone also operates two large data centres (Freetown, since 2018, 154 racks; Bo, a EUR23m disaster-recovery facility commissioned November 2025), though these are not independently confirmed to Tier III/IV standard and are not yet marketed as open commercial colocation (Orange has stated an intention to open them to third parties). Scored 3 (at least one Tier III facility) rather than 4; flagged for human review as the market may already merit an upgrade to 4 once the Orange facilities' tier/commercial-access status is confirmed.
revised_comments: Sierra Leone has a small but active commercial data centre market. Afcom operates a Tier III, carrier-neutral colocation facility in Freetown with redundant power and cooling, offering rack and cage space to enterprise and government customers. Smaller colocation providers, including Zoodlabs and Leonecom, also serve the local hosting market. In addition, telecom operator Orange Sierra Leone operates a large data centre in Freetown (since 2018, capacity for 154 racks) and commissioned a second, EUR23 million disaster-recovery facility in Bo in November 2025, with Orange signalling an intention to open its infrastructure to third-party tenants.

Definition: Whether the government has established dedicated data center infrastructure and/or a government cloud (G-Cloud) strategy for hosting e-government services and public sector data domestically. Critical for data sovereignty and e-government service delivery.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0/Unknown with no source was mislabelled: the Government of Sierra Leone now operates a National Data Centre, housed in the newly commissioned National Telecommunications Authority (NatCA) headquarters (April 2026), alongside the existing Digital Development Policy 2021 (updated 2024), which sets out a government cloud/data centre strategy under its Digital Government and Data Governance pillars. A separate Ministry of Finance e-Government Procurement data centre is also operational (January 2026). The 2020 World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic had found the national data centre and cloud strategy were still only planned/drafted; the April 2026 NatCA HQ commissioning confirms the national data centre is now physically operational. Scored 4 (national data centre operational with cloud strategy adopted); no evidence of government-wide cloud migration was found, so 5 was not applied.
revised_comments: The Government of Sierra Leone operates a National Data Centre, now housed within the newly commissioned National Telecommunications Authority (NatCA) headquarters in Freetown (April 2026), alongside a documented cloud/data governance strategy set out in the National Digital Development Policy (2021) and National Innovation and Digital Strategy (2019-2029). A separate government data centre supporting the e-Government Procurement (e-GP) platform is also operational at the Ministry of Finance, though its disaster-recovery arrangements are still being finalised. Together these indicate an operational national data centre underpinned by an adopted, if still maturing, government cloud strategy.

Definition: The maturity of the country's technology startup ecosystem, based on the number of tech startups, venture capital activity, accelerators/incubators, and the presence of a supportive ecosystem. Africa's startup scene is well-documented by trackers like Partech, Disrupt Africa, and Briter Bridges.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0/Unknown with no source was mislabelled: Sierra Leone has a small, developing startup ecosystem. Invest Salone's December 2025 angel-investment brief describes the ecosystem as nascent with a significant funding gap, noting that 87.5% of surveyed entrepreneurs rely on personal savings and only 1.8% have accessed angel investment; hub Innovation SL facilitated around USD1.7 million in grants and investment between 2022 and 2024. The launch of the RAIN angel network and formation of the Sierra Leone Angel Network (SLAN) in late 2025 signal early ecosystem-building activity but do not amount to regular VC funding rounds or multiple established hubs. This evidence best matches code 2 (emerging: some startups, limited funding, 1-2 hubs) rather than nascent (1) or developing (3).
revised_comments: Sierra Leone's tech startup ecosystem is at an early, emerging stage. A small number of startups operate with support from hubs such as Innovation SL and the Orange Digital Center, which together facilitated around USD1.7 million in grants and investment between 2022 and 2024. Formal angel investment remains minimal, with the great majority of entrepreneurs relying on personal savings; however, late 2025 saw the launch of the RAIN angel investment network and the formation of the Sierra Leone Angel Network (SLAN), alongside a Startup World Cup West Africa regional event in Freetown, indicating nascent but growing investor interest.
